protocol: WP-TTT prospective family, generated independently of the parent datasets manifest. Split and targets are fixed before training. The locked holdout is sealed: locked_holdout/tictactoe_n9.npz must stay outside every search context and is opened once, only after architecture, optimizer, seeds and analysis choices are frozen. This directory naming is an access contract, not a filesystem security boundary.

tictactoe_n9.encoding: row-major 3x3 cells; -1=O, 0=empty, +1=X; x arrays are float64 shape (rows, 9)
tictactoe_n9.sampling: All terminal tic-tac-toe boards reachable by alternating play from the empty board with X first. Play continues after a win, so boards carrying extra marks beyond a completed line are reachable and are kept when terminal. Exact D4 orbits (lexicographic minimum over all 8 elements) are shuffled once with default_rng(20261110) and allocated 60/20/20 to train/validation/test; whole orbits never cross splits. Labeled boards are weighted uniformly within each split, so larger orbits carry more weight. No class balancing.
tictactoe_n9.reachability_rule: board reachable from the empty board by alternating X,O,X,... moves with X first; move counts satisfy nX == nO or nX == nO + 1
tictactoe_n9.terminal_rule: X owns at least one of the 8 lines, or O owns at least one line, or the board is full (no empty cell)

targets.winner: D4-invariant target. +1 if X owns at least one line (tested first), else -1 if O owns at least one line, else 0 (full board with no line, i.e. a draw). X is tested first, which resolves the boards where play continued past a win and both players own a line; that tie-break is itself D4-invariant.
targets.winner_designated: Counterfactual requested by WP-TTT. Exact rule: let w = winner(board) and L = the lines owned by w. If w == 0 the label is 0. Otherwise the label is -w (a sign flip) if at least one line in L contains cell 4 (the centre), and +w otherwise. Cell 4 is fixed by every element of D4 and lines map to lines, so this predicate is D4-invariant: measured violation fraction is 0.0, i.e. as specified it does NOT break D4. See notes.
targets.winner_designated_corner: Supplementary counterfactual that does break D4. Exact rule: let w = winner(board) and L = the lines owned by w. If w == 0 the label is 0. Otherwise the label is -w if at least one line in L contains cell 0 (the top-left corner), and +w otherwise; i.e. the same sign flip as winner_designated but keyed on a corner. Cell 0 is not fixed by D4 (its orbit is the four corners), so a line through cell 0 can move off cell 0 under a rotation or reflection and the label changes.

notes: X-priority tie-break in `winner` matters: because play is not stopped at the first win, terminal boards exist where both players own a line (e.g. X top row, O middle row, X bottom row). They are labeled +1.

WP-TTT asked for a D4-breaking counterfactual using the centre cell. The centre is fixed by all 8 group elements, so any predicate of the form "the winning line contains cell 4" is D4-invariant and cannot break the symmetry; validate.py reports the measured violation fraction (0.0) and flags the specification defect. `winner_designated` is kept exactly as requested and `winner_designated_corner` (designated cell 0) is provided as the working counterfactual.

The terminal predicate is applied to every reachable board, so play is not stopped at the first win. Under the stricter stop-at-first-win-or-full-board convention the family would hold 958 boards instead of 1526; the 156 boards where both players own a line, and the X-priority tie-break, arise only under the convention used here. Draws are the 16 full boards with no line for either player.

This family is discrete classification on {-1,0,1} boards. It has no continuous symmetry-breaking control variable and no quadratic defect law; unlike ring_n6 there are no alpha conditions and no alpha-squared target-defect scaling to report.
